chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Wallad al-Hannat, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Two men were brought to Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him), each of whom had accused his companion of adultery in his body. So he (peace be upon him) repelled the Hadd penalty from both of them and reprimanded them.'

key_terms.بَدَنِهِ: in his body, referring to the physical act or evidence
key_terms.عَزَّرَهُمَا: he reprimanded or punished them with Ta'zir (discretionary punishment)
key_terms.قَذَفَ: to accuse or charge, specifically in the context of legal accusation (Qadhf)

ai.seo_question: How did Imam Ali exercise judicial discretion in cases of mutual accusation of adultery?
ai.summary: This incident from al-Kafi highlights Imam Ali’s judicial discretion (Ta'zir) by suspending the fixed Hadd punishment for Zina due to the specific context of mutual accusation and bodily evidence, rather than the standard four-witness requirement. It underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that the application of penal codes is subject to the judge’s assessment of circumstances, allowing for flexible reprimand when strict evidentiary thresholds for Hadd are not fully met. This reflects the broader legal theory that Ta'zir serves as a complementary mechanism to Hadd, ensuring justice adapts to the nuances of each case.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Wallad Al hannat who said,

‘I heard Abu Abdullahasws saying, ‘They came to Amir Al-Momineenasws with two men, each one of them had slandered his companion with the adultery in his body. So heasws staved off the Penalty (Hadd) from both of them, and reprimanded them both’.
